2|_A D&D 5e (2024) adventure for 4–5 3rd-level characters_
3|
4|A few miles beyond the village of **Haverton**, something ancient has emerged from beneath the earth.
5|
6|For months, hunters and woodsmen have whispered about a stone doorway that appeared at the foot of a grassy hill beyond the forest. No storm uncovered it. No landslide exposed it. One morning, it simply existed.
7|
8|A dozen adventurers have entered since.
9|
10|Only one returned.
11|
12|Half-starved and barely coherent, the survivor spoke of stone guardians, corpses crawling from their tombs, and terrible glass vessels filled with swirling darkness.
13|
14|But one detail disturbed the people of Haverton more than any other.
15|
16|He swore that after his companions died, **he could still hear them screaming from inside the tomb.**
17|
18|The tomb is the hidden laboratory of **Opendis**, a necromancer who discovered a means of capturing mortal souls and storing them within enchanted vessels.
19|
20|Opendis has disappeared.
21|
22|His experiments have not.
23|
24|---
25|
26|# Adventure Hook
27|
28|The characters hear about the tomb while staying in Haverton.
29|
30|Several families are desperate to learn what happened to the missing explorers. A local scholar is equally interested in the strange structure and offers the characters **100 gp** if they can determine its purpose and return with evidence.
31|
32|The sole survivor, **Edric Vale**, can also be questioned.
33|
34|Edric remembers little clearly, but repeatedly warns:
35|
36|> "Don't touch the jars. Gods above, don't touch the jars."
37|
38|He remembers seeing his companions die—and then hearing their voices begging him for help from somewhere deeper inside the tomb.
39|
40|---
41|
42|# Reaching the Tomb
43|
44|The tomb lies roughly **two days from Haverton** through dense forest.
45|
46|The journey doesn't need to be a full wilderness adventure. Instead, use it to establish the increasingly unnatural atmosphere surrounding the tomb.
47|
48|During the second day, animals become scarce.
49|
50|Birdsong disappears.
51|
52|That evening, characters occasionally hear whispers between the trees.
53|
54|A character who succeeds on a **DC 12 Wisdom (Perception)** check hears fragments:
55|
56|_"Come closer..."_
57|
58|_"It hurts..."_
59|
60|_"Please..."_
61|
62|_"There's room for you too..."_
63|
64|These aren't ghosts wandering the forest. They are psychic echoes emanating from the Jars of Souls.
65|
66|---
67|
68|# 1. The Entrance
69|
70|A grassy clearing surrounds a large hill. Built into its base is an ancient stone doorway leading downward.
71|
72|Weathered stairs descend into darkness.
73|
74|Characters approaching within 30 feet hear faint whispers from below.
75|
76|A **DC 12 Intelligence (Arcana or Religion)** check reveals that these aren't ordinary haunting manifestations. Something beneath the hill is magically attracting or containing spirits.
77|
78|The stairs descend approximately 40 feet before reaching Area 2.
79|
80|---
81|
82|# 2. The Landing
83|
84|A circular chamber marks the true entrance to the complex.
85|
86|An enormous necromantic rune has been carved into the floor.
87|
88|Four stone pedestals surround it, each holding a grotesque idol depicting a forgotten entity devouring humanoid spirits.
89|
90|A successful **DC 12 Intelligence (Arcana or Religion)** check identifies the circle's purpose:
91|
92|**It channels spiritual energy toward the center of the tomb.**
93|
94|The large double doors leading to Area 7 have no handles or visible locks.
95|
96|Magic seals them.
97|
98|Casting _Detect Magic_ reveals strong Necromancy and Abjuration magic.
99|
100|The doors open only when someone speaks:
101|
102|**"Syvethis."**
103|
104|The characters can discover the command word in Area 6.
105|
106|Attempting to force the doors open automatically fails.
107|
108|---
109|
110|# 3. Immortal Guardians
111|
112|Two chambers contain Opendis's earliest successful Jars of Souls.
113|
114|Each room contains:
115|
116|- Two stone guardian statues
117|    
118|- One Jar of Souls
119|    
120|- Ancient necromantic inscriptions
121|    
122|
123|When a creature approaches within 10 feet of the jar, the statues animate.
124|
125|### Encounter
126|
127|Use **2 Animated Armors** in each room.
128|
129|However, the guardians aren't interested in pursuing intruders through the dungeon.
130|
131|They exist solely to protect the jar.
132|
133|If characters retreat from the chamber, the constructs return to their original positions after 1 minute.
134|
135|### The Jar
136|
137|A black ceramic vessel rests upon a stone pedestal.
138|
139|Ghostly faces occasionally push outward from its surface before disappearing.
140|
141|Each jar contains several tortured souls.
142|
143|Touching it causes the creature to hear dozens of overlapping whispers.
144|
145|The jar is worth approximately **300 gp** to the right buyer, although selling such an object should have obvious moral consequences.
146|
147|### Breaking the Jar
148|
149|AC 12  
150|HP 10  
151|Immune: Poison, Psychic
152|
153|Destroying the jar releases the souls trapped inside.
154|
155|A wave of spectral energy fills the chamber.
156|
157|Every creature within 10 feet must make a **DC 12 Wisdom saving throw**.
158|
159|On a failure, the creature is **Frightened until the end of its next turn**.
160|
161|The spirits then disappear.
162|
163|A character proficient in Arcana or Religion realizes the souls have finally been allowed to pass into the afterlife.
164|
165|### Taking the Jar
166|
167|The characters may instead carry the intact vessel.
168|
169|Doing so could attract the attention of necromancers, undead creatures, religious authorities—or Opendis himself.
170|
171|---
172|
173|# 4. Forsaken Sarcophagi
174|
175|Several sarcophagi line the corridors surrounding the central chamber.
176|
177|They initially appear dormant.
178|
179|They aren't.
180|
181|The tomb's guardians awaken whenever someone interferes with Opendis's experiments.
182|
183|The **first time the characters move, damage, or destroy a Jar of Souls**, two nearby sarcophagi burst open.
184|
185|### Encounter
186|
187|**2 Ghouls** emerge.
188|
189|Afterward, the remaining sarcophagi occasionally rattle or produce scratching sounds, but don't immediately open.
190|
191|When the characters eventually open the doors to Area 7, **2 additional Ghouls** emerge from the remaining sarcophagi.
192|
193|This splits the original eight-monster encounter into manageable battles while maintaining the feeling that the entire tomb is waking around them.
194|
195|---
196|
197|# 5. East Libraries
198|
199|The northern library has largely collapsed.
200|
201|Rotten books cover the floor beneath fallen shelves.
202|
203|Most are unreadable.
204|
205|The southern library is protected by a locked wooden door.
206|
207|**DC 13 Dexterity (Sleight of Hand using Thieves' Tools)** opens the lock.
208|
209|Alternatively:
210|
211|AC 15  
212|HP 15
213|
214|Inside are Opendis's research notes.
215|
216|Characters spending at least 10 minutes examining them learn:
217|
218|### Opendis
219|
220|Opendis was a powerful mage obsessed with the boundary between life and death.
221|
222|He believed souls weren't merely spiritual entities.
223|
224|They were **energy**.
225|
226|Energy that could be collected.
227|
228|Stored.
229|
230|And eventually consumed.
231|
232|He constructed this laboratory to develop vessels capable of trapping souls before they could reach the afterlife.
233|
234|His writings repeatedly refer to something called:
235|
236|**"The Great Working."**
237|
238|Apparently, Opendis intended to gather hundreds—perhaps thousands—of souls to power a ritual.
239|
240|Exactly what that ritual would accomplish isn't explained.
241|
242|Opendis's current whereabouts are unknown.
243|
244|---
245|
246|# 6. West Libraries
247|
248|The southern library has collapsed.
249|
250|The northern chamber remains intact but locked.
251|
252|The door requires a **DC 13 Dexterity (Sleight of Hand using Thieves' Tools)** check or can simply be destroyed.
253|
254|Inside are records describing the tomb's magical protections.
255|
256|Characters learn that Opendis concealed the entire structure using an enormous illusion and transmutation ritual.
257|
258|The enchantment was designed to last for decades.
259|
260|The tomb's recent appearance means the spell has finally failed.
261|
262|More importantly, they discover the command used to enter Opendis's ritual chamber:
263|
264|## SYVETHIS
265|
266|Speaking the word near the doors in Area 2 causes ancient mechanisms to grind beneath the floor.
267|
268|The central doors slowly open.
269|
270|---
271|
272|# 7. Ritual Chamber
273|
274|The doors open onto an enormous circular chamber.
275|
276|Broken ritual equipment covers the floor.
277|
278|Black candles have melted into strange shapes.
279|
280|Silver wire forms incomplete magical circles.
281|
282|And surrounding the central ritual platform are **four Jars of Souls**.
283|
284|Unlike the previous vessels, these are active.
285|
286|Ghostly figures visibly swirl within them.
287|
288|Some pound desperately against the inside of the glass.
289|
290|Among them are the souls of the adventurers who disappeared from Haverton.
291|
292|As the characters enter, spectral guardians rise from the floor.
293|
294|### Encounter
295|
296|Use:
297|
298|**2 Specters**
299|
300|and
301|
302|**1 Skeleton**
303|
304|The skeleton wears the remains of ceremonial robes and acts as the ritual chamber's physical caretaker.
305|
306|The Specters are bound spirits forced to defend the laboratory.
307|
308|### Soul-Fueled Guardians
309|
310|The jars power the undead.
311|
312|At **Initiative Count 20**, one intact jar emits a pulse of necrotic energy.
313|
314|One undead creature in the chamber gains **5 Temporary Hit Points**.
315|
316|The characters can prevent this by destroying the jars during combat.
317|
318|### Destroying a Jar
319|
320|AC 12  
321|HP 10
322|
323|When destroyed, its trapped souls erupt outward.
324|
325|Every undead creature within 15 feet takes **1d6 Radiant damage**.
326|
327|This gives the players an important tactical choice:
328|
329|Fight the guardians normally...
330|
331|or start smashing the very artifacts they came to investigate.
332|
333|---
334|
335|# The Lost Adventurers
336|
337|After the battle, the characters recognize several spirits within the remaining jars from descriptions given by people in Haverton.
338|
339|These are the missing explorers.
340|
341|The characters have three choices.
342|
343|### Release Them
344|
345|Destroying the jars allows the spirits to pass onward.
346|
347|For several moments, translucent figures appear throughout the chamber.
348|
349|Some simply disappear.
350|
351|Others thank the characters.
352|
353|One whispers:
354|
355|_"He'll come back for them."_
356|
357|Then the chamber falls silent.
358|
359|### Take the Jars
360|
361|The characters can instead remove the jars.
362|
363|Each could theoretically be worth **300 gp** to collectors of forbidden magic.
364|
365|Possessing one, however, is both dangerous and morally questionable.
366|
367|### Study Them
368|
369|A character who spends 10 minutes examining a jar and succeeds on a **DC 14 Intelligence (Arcana)** check realizes the vessels could potentially be modified.
370|
371|They don't merely contain souls.
372|
373|They can **transfer their spiritual energy into another ritual or magical object**.
374|
375|Whatever Opendis intended to do here required an enormous amount of power.
376|
377|---
378|
379|# 8. Secret Vault — Opendis's Wealth
380|
381|A hidden stone button can be discovered with a **DC 14 Wisdom (Perception)** or **DC 12 Intelligence (Investigation)** check.
382|
383|Pressing it causes part of the wall to slide open.
384|
385|Inside is Opendis's emergency treasury.
386|
387|The characters find:
388|
389|- 180 gp
390|    
391|- 420 sp
392|    
393|- 4 bloodstones worth 50 gp each
394|    
395|- An ornate silver chalice worth 75 gp
396|    
397|- 2 Potions of Healing
398|    
399|
400|A small locked box also contains one of Opendis's personal seals.
401|
402|The symbol depicts:
403|
404|**An open hand holding a screaming skull.**
405|
406|This symbol can later identify Opendis's followers or other laboratories.
407|
408|---
409|
410|# 9. Secret Vault — Arcane Storage
411|
412|Another secret button opens this chamber.
413|
414|Inside are shelves containing magical supplies and unfinished experiments.
415|
416|The characters discover three spell scrolls:
417|
418|- **Scroll of Detect Magic**
419|    
420|- **Scroll of Protection from Evil and Good**
421|    
422|- **Scroll of Gentle Repose**
423|    
424|
425|They also find a peculiar black crystal.
426|
427|A successful **DC 13 Intelligence (Arcana)** check reveals that the crystal once contained spiritual energy similar to the Jars of Souls.
428|
429|Unlike the jars, however...
430|
431|**This crystal is empty.**
432|
433|Someone used it.
434|
435|---
436|
437|# Ending the Adventure
438|
439|When the characters leave the tomb, the whispers surrounding the clearing are gone if they released the trapped souls.
440|
441|The forest feels alive again.
442|
443|Birds return.
444|
445|Wind moves through the trees.
446|
447|Back in Haverton, the families of the missing adventurers finally learn what happened to their loved ones.
448|
449|If the characters released their souls, the community considers them heroes.
450|
451|But the discoveries within the tomb raise a much larger question.
452|
453|Opendis spent decades gathering souls.
454|
455|He constructed an entire laboratory.
456|
457|He created magical vessels capable of stealing the dead from the afterlife.
458|
459|And yet...
460|
461|**Opendis isn't here.**
462|
463|His ritual was never completed.
464|
465|His most important research is missing.
466|
467|And one of his soul-storage crystals has already been emptied.
468|
469|Somewhere in the world, Opendis may still be alive.
470|
471|And eventually, he will discover that someone has broken into his tomb.
472|
473|---
474|
475|# Scaling the Adventure
476|
477|### 3 Characters
478|
479|Remove one Animated Armor from one of the Area 3 encounters.
480|
481|The Ritual Chamber contains **2 Specters only**.
482|
483|### 4 Characters
484|
485|Run the adventure as written.
486|
487|### 5 Characters
488|
489|Run the adventure as written, but give the Ritual Chamber skeleton **2 additional Skeleton allies**.
490|
491|---
492|
493|# Adventure Rewards
494|
495|If the characters explore most of the dungeon, defeat the guardians, discover Opendis's research, and resolve the fate of the trapped souls, they have accomplished a significant adventure appropriate for 3rd level.
496|
497|Recommended rewards:
498|
499|**100 gp** from the Haverton scholar.
500|
501|Approximately **450–700 gp worth of treasure** throughout the dungeon.
502|
503|**2 Potions of Healing.**
504|
505|**3 low-level spell scrolls.**
506|
507|Most importantly, they discover **Opendis and the Great Working**, providing a ready-made villain and plot thread for later adventures.
508|
509|## Future Hook: Opendis Returns
510|
511|Don't have Opendis attack immediately.
512|
513|Weeks or even months later, the characters discover the symbol of the **hand holding the screaming skull** somewhere else.
514|
515|Perhaps on a corpse.
516|
517|Perhaps in another abandoned laboratory.
518|
519|Perhaps carried by someone asking questions about the adventurers who entered the tomb near Haverton.
520|
521|Eventually they learn the truth:
522|
523|**Opendis knows their names.**"
    }
  ]

      "content": "1|# The Tenebrous Stone-r
2|
3|A one-shot for a level 3 meme-team of adventurers in Stickyickistan! Based on the free adventure, *Forgotten Realms: The Tenebrous Stone*.
4|
5|---
6|
7|# Adventure Hook
8|
9|The **[[Blacklung Quarry]]**, one of Stickyickistan's oldest sources of Arcanite, ceased operations a couple months ago due to supernatural happenings. One day the laborers ventured down into the subterranean mine, but none ever returned. Every time a few more would go down, they too would not return. Yet each night, the sound of pickaxes still echoes from deep within the quarry.
10|
11|About two ten days ago the quarry's owner, the dwarf **[[Roggan Stonebrah]]**, sent **Brother Highwind** of the **[[Order of the Emerald Breath]]** to investigate, but the monk also never returned. Ever since Brother Highwind's disappearance, a foul-smelling [[Arcannabis]] smoke drifts up the elevator shaft from the mine below. Those who've huffed the stank speak of horrific visions and waking nightmares.
12|
13|A very desperate Roggan now offers **300 gp** to anyone willing to enter the quarry, find Brother Highwind, and put an end to whatever evil has taken root within. The bounty has been posted to the **Free League of Stickyickistan's ([[Free League of Stickyickistan]])** bounty board called **[[The Rolling Papers]]**. One of your characters has taken the contract, and recruited the rest of the characters to take on the quest with them.
14|
15|---
16|
17|# Character Creation
18|
19|- Create a **Level 3** character.
20|- Any official species, class, or background is welcome.
21|- I have some suggestions for you to ignore below.
22|- Please roll stats before day of, otherwise use standard array.
23|- Your character should have a reason to take on dangerous work and cooperate with the rest of the party.
24|
25|## Stickyickistanian Backgrounds
26|
27|- A member of the **[[Tribunal Highblade Coalition]] (THC)**, the premier mercenary house of Stickyickistan. Generally lawful good followers of the Faith of Sacred Flame religion. Every class can work with this faction.
28|- An employee of **[[The Seekers of the Vein]]**. More than just a Mining & Jeweler's Guild, the Seekers are an economic empire, fueling Stickyickistan's Magitech advancements. Generally neutral good non-religious folk. Makes most sense for artificer, or wizard, but get creative.
29|- A rogue member of the **[[Ashen Shadow Society]] (ASS)**, a clandestine bounty hunting guild that "doesn't exist", and loves to collect relics, bounties, and monsters. Pose as a member of The Seekers, or a sell sword from THC. Generally lawful neutral folks from all paths of life. You cannot be evil aligned.
30|- A member of the **Order of the Emerald Breath**, could work for monks, druids, and maybe a cleric. Lawful good people with no exceptions and Followers of the Old Faiths.
31|- Feel free to come up with your own!
32|### Lore Context
33|
34|- Followers of **[[The Faith of the Sacred Flame]] are generally the [[Human Colonialism|colonist]] settler population that used religion as a justification to purge the native population of Stickyickistan. They are also a majority Human, but there are some Elves, Dwarves, and Dragonborn.
35|- **[[The Old Faiths]]** are what the settler population calls any neutral to good faith other than the Sacred Flame. There is some tension between followers of the Sacred Flame and the Old Faiths, but relations have been mending over the years.
36|- **[[Shadow Faiths]]** are what the settlers call any evil aligned faith. Both followers of the Old Faiths, and the Sacred Flame can agree on one thing. Followers of the Shadow Faiths.
37|- **THC** and **ASS** actively oppose each other, and the **Seekers of the Vein** work with both. Depends on what they are okay with the law seeing.
38|
39|## Helpful Skills
40|
41|Characters proficient in **Arcana, Investigation, Nature, Perception, Religion, and/or Survival** will find opportunities to shine.
42|
43|## Magic Items
44|
45|Each character can choose **1 Uncommon**, and **1 Common** item from the lists below, as well as **1 zip of a novice strain of Arcannabis** from the list below. This is entirely optional. Potions count as your **1 Uncommon** item.

83|### Arcannabis
84|
85|Do not use the homebrewed magic items in D&D Beyond labeled **"Arcannabis"**. They are deprecated, and don't fit the setting anymore.
86|
87|- Grave Gaze #4 (Undead Eyes)
88|	- Know the location of any undead within a radius around you that isn't protected from divination magic. The radius increases with rarity.
89|	- **Radius:** 10 ft

98|- Brainwreck (Aberration Brain)
99|	- Can communicate telepathically with creatures within **30 ft** of you. You must be able to see the creature and share a language to communicate in this way.

      "content": "1|# Type
2|- Faith-Based Organization
3|- [[The Old Faiths]]
4|- Lawful Good
5|- Guardians of Natural Balance
6|
7|## Headquarters
8|- The Emerald Sanctuary
9|- [[Stickyickistan]]
10|
11|## Symbol
12|- A green cannabis leaf encircling a pair of open hands, with a single emerald-colored wisp of smoke rising from its center.
13|
14|## Motto
15|> **"Every breath is a blessing."**
16|
17|## Leadership
18|- High Herbalist *(leader of the Order)*
19|- Circle of Verdant Elders
20|- Emerald Brothers and Sisters
21|
22|## Allies
23|- [[Tribunal Highblade Coalition]]
24|- Followers of [[Ashalla]]
25|- Druids, monks, rangers, and some clerics.
26|- Communities that respect nature and responsible [[Arcannabis Cultivation]]
27|
28|## Rivals
29|- [[Blossom Union]] — respected fellow servants of nature, but frustratingly insular, traditional, and unwilling to let the Order help manage [[Springarden]] or its fey-touched resources.
30|
31|## Enemies
32|- Necromancers
33|- Those who corrupt Arcannabis through profane magic
34|- Poachers and those who exploit the natural world
35|
36|## Ideals
37|- **Balance.** Nature provides, but only to those who respect it.
38|- **Compassion.** Healing should be offered before judgment.
39|- **Stewardship.** Arcannabis is a sacred gift, not a weapon.
40|- **Community.** No one should suffer alone.
41|
42|## Beliefs
43|- Arcannabis is a divine gift meant to heal body, mind, and spirit.
44|- Every strain has a purpose when cultivated with care.
45|- Corrupted strains are an affront to the natural order and must be destroyed.
46|- Death is a natural part of life and should never be perverted through undeath.
47|- Sacred gardens should serve living communities, not become sealed relics guarded by tradition alone.
48|
49|## Duties
50|- Heal the sick and injured.
51|- Bless and cultivate sacred Arcannabis gardens.
52|- Educate communities on responsible cultivation and use.
53|- Purify corrupted plants, soil, and magical blight.
54|- Investigate reports of unnatural diseases, curses, or monstrous outbreaks.
55|
56|## Ranks
57|- Initiate
58|- Herbalist
59|- Emerald Brother / Emerald Sister
60|- Verdant Warden
61|- High Herbalist
62|
63|## Members
64|- Clerics
65|- Druids
66|- Monks
67|- Rangers
68|- Herbalists
69|- Alchemists
70|- Volunteers devoted to community service
71|
72|## Personality
73|Members of the Order are known for their calm demeanor, endless patience, and willingness to help anyone in need. They often speak softly, encourage others to slow down and breathe, and believe that understanding is stronger than violence. While peaceful by nature, they become fiercely determined when confronting those who spread undeath or corrupt the gifts of nature.
74|
75|## Short History
76|The Order of the Emerald Breath was founded after a group of healers discovered the remarkable restorative properties of Arcannabis. Rather than treating the plant as a commodity, they embraced it as a sacred gift capable of easing pain, calming troubled minds, and bringing communities together.
77|
78|Over generations, the Order became one of Stickyickistan's most respected charitable organizations, maintaining free gardens, healing sanctuaries, and educational halls across the island. Their members travel far and wide to provide aid during disasters, teach responsible cultivation, and preserve rare strains for future generations.
79|
80|The Order considers the corruption of Arcannabis to be among the greatest crimes imaginable. Whether the blight stems from demonic influence, necromancy, or reckless experimentation, its members dedicate themselves to cleansing the land and ensuring the Emerald Breath continues to bring life rather than death.
81|
82|Their rivalry with the [[Blossom Union]] began as a disagreement over access to [[Springarden]]. The Order believes Springarden’s sacred plants, healing springs, and fey-touched crossings should be studied, shared, and carefully used to help communities across [[Stickyickistan]]. The Blossom Union believes the garden must be protected first, even if that means refusing outside healers, scholars, and cultivators. Neither side sees the other as evil, but both believe the other is dangerously wrong.
83|
84|## Notable Members
85|- **Brother Highwind** – A compassionate monk who volunteered to investigate the corruption beneath Blacklung Quarry in the adventure [[The Tenebrous Stone-r]].
86|
87|## Favorite Quotes
88|> "Every breath is a blessing."
89|
90|> "The strongest medicine is compassion."
91|
92|> "Nature always finds a way—our duty is to help it."
93|
94|> "Life grows. Death feeds it. Undeath steals from both."",

For months, hunters and woodsmen have whispered about a stone doorway that appeared at the foot of a grassy hill beyond the forest. No storm uncovered it. No landslide exposed it. One morning, it simply existed.

A dozen adventurers have entered since.

One morning, it simply existed. The doorway lies on an old service road once used to move ore toward [[Blacklung Quarry]].

A dozen adventurers have entered since.

value.newText:
They also find a peculiar black crystal.

A successful **DC 13 Intelligence (Arcana or Religion)** check reveals that the crystal once contained spiritual energy similar to the Jars of Souls. It was not merely a storage device: the cult used crystals like this to feed stolen souls into a larger necromantic working.

Unlike the jars, however...

**This crystal is empty.**

Someone used it. A character who knows of [[The Tenebrous Stone-r]] recognizes the residue as similar to the energy released beneath [[Blacklung Quarry]], suggesting that the cult moved the experiment there after abandoning Opendis’s laboratory.

      "content": "437|# Ending the Adventure

439|When the characters leave the tomb, the whispers surrounding the clearing are gone if they released the trapped souls.

441|The forest feels alive again.
442|
443|Birds return.
444|
445|Wind moves through the trees.
446|
447|Back in Haverton, the families of the missing adventurers finally learn what happened to their loved ones.
448|
449|If the characters released their souls, the community considers them heroes.
450|
451|But the discoveries within the tomb raise a much larger question.
452|
453|Opendis spent decades gathering souls.
454|
455|He constructed an entire laboratory.
456|
457|He created magical vessels capable of stealing the dead from the afterlife.
458|
459|And yet...

messages.content:
`Jars of Souls.md` is now integrated into Stickyickistan and connected to *The Tenebrous Stone-r*.

Key changes:
- Haverton is now a Stickyickistanian mining settlement.
- The tomb lies along an old ore road connected to [[Blacklung Quarry]].
- Opendis is an arcanist serving [[Orcus]].
- A hidden Orcus cult among Stickyickistan’s mining interests funded the soul experiments.
- [[Arcanite]] is used to power the cult’s mass-resurrection ritual.
- The [[Seekers of the Vein]] now have a reason to investigate the tomb.
- The empty black crystal links the tomb’s experiments to the supernatural activity beneath [[Blacklung Quarry]].
- Opendis’s seal identifies the Orcus cult and foreshadows future encounters.
- The ending now establishes that the party has interrupted the cult’s supply line rather than ended the threat.

      "content": "1|Doobius House is a village in [[The Outback]] of [[Stickyickistan]] inhabited by indigenous [[Twothirdlings]], and a few full Halflings. This village was founded in the earliest years of [[Human Colonialism]] and is named after the head of [[House Highblade]], and a great military leader of old, [[Duke Doobius Highblade]]. A thriving village in its hay day, it boasted the highest population of any inland settlement. In the current day, it is a run-down village with a very similar population to what it had in its prime. The growth of the town stagnated once the frontier, and native populations had been conquered / assimilated and there was no longer a need for a major inland post.
2|
3|# History
4|
5|During it's hay day the town had a bustling economy relative to the time. Many adventurers would pass through the village streets, and although it is nothing like the city of Stickyickistan today, the village had plenty of options for commerce.
6|
7|# POIs
8|
9|### [[Hotbox Inn & Tavern]]
10|
11|Owner: [[Barnabas Huggins]]
12|
13|Players can rest here, and buy food, drink, and novice level [[Arcannabis]] strains from Barnabas. Barnabas also may have some info about happenings around the town. He can not make Arcannabis strains he just sells it.
14|
15|**Barnabas Huggins** is a stout, rosy-cheeked man in his mid-50s, with thinning auburn hair combed stubbornly across his head and a laugh that seems to roll out of his belly like a thunderclap. He dresses in plain but well-kept clothes, his apron always dusted with flour or ale stains. Barnabas is a natural storyteller—half of what he says is truth, the other half is so exaggerated that even he forgets where the line is. He has a warm, booming hospitality, but he also has a sharp eye; nothing that happens under his roof escapes his notice. Regulars know him as a man who can get you anything—whether it’s a good smoke, a hot meal, or a whispered rumor—provided you’ve got coin and keep out of trouble.
16|
17|Voice & Mannerisms
18|- Loud, booming laugh that fills the room.
19|- Talks in long-winded stories, often blending truth with exaggeration.
20|- Always wiping his apron with a rag, though it never seems clean.
21|- Winks knowingly when sharing a rumor or deal.
22|Attitude
23|- Warm, welcoming, and larger-than-life.
24|- Sharp-eyed despite his jolly demeanor—nothing slips past him.
25|- Pragmatic: willing to deal in food, drink, smoke, and gossip if coin’s on the table.
26|- Protective of his inn’s peace—rowdiness is tolerated, but troublemakers get the boot.
27|Interactions
28|- Greets newcomers like old friends, drawing them into tales of “what really happened” years ago.
29|- Sells food, drink, and novice-level Arcannabis strains, but insists he’s “no grower, just a seller.”
30|- Slips rumors or local news into casual conversation, often for the price of a pint.
31|- Knows how to balance being everyone’s friend with being the quiet watcher of the room.
32|
33|### [[Burial Barrow]]
34|
35|This is an ancient burial place that the pioneers of the village have appropriated as their own.
36|
37|### [[Celestial Chapel]]
38|
39|This is a special church built by the clergy specifically for training new missionaries, and "converting" natives. Not where the common folk go to pray.
40|
41|### [[Grim Forest]] Edge
42|
43|The origins of the grim forest are not known. The only knowledge of this place is held by indigenous elders that haven't lost their oral history traditions. Evil plants, and some undead roam this forest. The edge of the woods is guarded by an ancient awakened radiant tree.
44|
45|### [[Doobius House Greengrocer]]
46|
47|Owner: [[Matilda "Tilly" Cabbagewhistle]]
48|
49|Tilly is a sprightly halfling woman in her late 60s, though she insists she’s “still young enough to outrun a carrot thief.” She’s got wiry gray hair tied back in a messy bun, sharp green eyes, and hands stained from years of pulling weeds and weighing apples. She’s endlessly chatty—every purchase comes with at least two local rumors and three unsolicited cooking tips. Beneath her cheerful demeanor, she’s fiercely protective of her stall and her produce, wielding her broom with alarming speed when would-be thieves try their luck.
50|
51|Voice & Mannerisms
52|- Fast-talking, cheerful, always has a story or rumor to share.
53|- Sharp green eyes that miss very little.
54|- Waves her hands when speaking, often holding a vegetable for emphasis.
55|- Keeps a broom nearby and isn’t shy about brandishing it.
56|Attitude
57|- Energetic and sprightly despite her age.
58|- Fiercely protective of her produce and her stall.
59|- Warm and neighborly, though a little nosy.
60|- Prideful about freshness and quality—takes offense at haggling.
61|Interactions
62|- Every sale comes with gossip, cooking advice, or both.
63|- Treats regular customers like family, but expects respect.
64|- Chases thieves with broom in hand—swift and merciless in defense of her goods.
65|- Has a soft spot for children, often slipping them fruit for free.
66|
67|### Town Square
68|
69|In the center of the town square there is a Fountain of holy water that is blessed by priests daily and dawn and dusk. Both human and halfling commoners will come here to pray. The fountain is surrounded by stone brick buildings, and an elevated concourse leading to a some local businesses. These businesses include:
70|
71| - Butcher
72| - florist
73| - tailor
74| - guard post
75| - bookshop
76|
77|### [[Hidden Grove]] "Witch" Hut
78|

2|_A D&D 5e (2024) adventure for 4–5 3rd-level characters_
3|
4|A few miles beyond the Stickyickistanian mining settlement of **Haverton**, something ancient has emerged from beneath the earth.
5|
6|For months, hunters and woodsmen have whispered about a stone doorway that appeared at the foot of a grassy hill beyond the forest. No storm uncovered it. No landslide exposed it. One morning, it simply existed. The doorway lies on an old service road once used to move ore toward [[Blacklung Quarry]].
7|
8|A dozen adventurers have entered since.
9|
10|Only one returned.
11|
12|Half-starved and barely coherent, the survivor spoke of stone guardians, corpses crawling from their tombs, and terrible glass vessels filled with swirling darkness.
13|
14|But one detail disturbed the people of Haverton more than any other.
15|
16|He swore that after his companions died, **he could still hear them screaming from inside the tomb.**
17|
18|The tomb is the hidden laboratory of **[[Opendis]]**, a necromancer and arcanist of [[Orcus]] who discovered a means of capturing mortal souls and storing them within enchanted vessels. Opendis was supplied by a hidden Orcus cult operating among Stickyickistan’s mining interests; the cult sought to turn the island’s abundant [[Arcanite]] into a power source for a mass resurrection ritual.
19|
20|Opendis has disappeared.
21|
22|His experiments have not.
23|
24|---
25|
26|# Adventure Hook
27|
28|The characters hear about the tomb while staying in Haverton.
29|
30|Several families are desperate to learn what happened to the missing explorers. A local scholar from the [[Seekers of the Vein]] is equally interested in the strange structure: the old service road once connected to [[Blacklung Quarry]], and the tomb’s stonework contains traces of refined [[Arcanite]]. The scholar offers the characters **100 gp** if they can determine the structure’s purpose and return with evidence.
31|
32|The sole survivor, **Edric Vale**, can also be questioned.
33|
34|Edric remembers little clearly, but repeatedly warns:
35|
36|> "Don't touch the jars. Gods above, don't touch the jars."
37|
38|He remembers seeing his companions die—and then hearing their voices begging him for help from somewhere deeper inside the tomb.
39|
40|---",

11|
12|Half-starved and barely coherent, the survivor spoke of stone guardians, corpses crawling from their tombs, and terrible glass vessels filled with swirling darkness.
13|
14|But one detail disturbed the people of [[Doobius House]] more than any other.
15|
16|He swore that after his companions died, **he could still hear them screaming from inside the tomb.**
17|
18|The tomb is the hidden laboratory of **[[Opendis]]**, a necromancer and arcanist of [[Orcus]] who discovered a means of capturing mortal souls and storing them within enchanted vessels. Opendis was supplied by a hidden Orcus cult operating among Stickyickistan’s mining interests; the cult sought to turn the island’s abundant [[Arcanite]] into a power source for a mass raise dead ritual.
19|
20|Opendis has disappeared.
21|
22|His experiments have not.
23|
24|---
25|
26|# Adventure Hook
27|
28|The characters hear about the tomb while staying in Haverton.
29|
30|Several families are desperate to learn what happened to the missing explorers. A local scholar from the [[Seekers of the Vein]] is equally interested in the strange structure: the old service road once connected to [[Blacklung Quarry]], and the tomb’s stonework contains traces of refined [[Arcanite]]. The scholar offers the characters **100 gp** if they can determine the structure’s purpose and return with evidence.
31|
32|The sole survivor, **Edric Vale**, can also be questioned.
33|
34|Edric remembers little clearly, but repeatedly warns:
35|
36|> "Don't touch the jars. Gods above, don't touch the jars."
37|
38|He remembers seeing his companions die—and then hearing their voices begging him for help from somewhere deeper inside the tomb.
39|

434|# Ending the Adventure
435|
436|When the characters leave the tomb, the whispers surrounding the clearing are gone if they released the trapped souls.
437|
438|The forest feels alive again.
439|
440|Birds return.
441|
442|Wind moves through the trees.
443|
444|Back in Haverton, the families of the missing adventurers finally learn what happened to their loved ones.
445|
446|If the characters released their souls, the community considers them heroes.
447|
448|But the discoveries within the tomb raise a much larger question. The Orcus cult did not build this laboratory for Opendis alone. They were using it as a collection site, then funneling the harvested souls and Arcanite toward the ritual beneath [[Blacklung Quarry]].
449|
450|Opendis spent decades gathering souls.
451|
452|He constructed an entire laboratory.
453|
454|He created magical vessels capable of stealing the dead from the afterlife.
455|

457|
458|**Opendis isn't here.**
459|
460|His ritual was never completed.
461|
462|His most important research is missing.
463|
464|And one of his soul-storage crystals has already been emptied.
465|
466|Somewhere in the world, Opendis may still be alive.
467|
468|And eventually, he will discover that someone has broken into his tomb.

491|
492|If the characters explore most of the dungeon, defeat the guardians, discover Opendis's research, and resolve the fate of the trapped souls, they have accomplished a significant adventure appropriate for 3rd level.

497|

499|
500|**2 Potions of Healing.**
501|
502|**3 low-level spell scrolls.**
503|
504|Most importantly, they discover **Opendis, the Orcus cult, and the Great Working**, providing a ready-made villain and plot thread for later adventures. 2|_A D&D 5e (2024) adventure for 4–5 3rd-level characters_
3|
4|A few miles beyond the village of **[[Doobius House]]**, something ancient has emerged from beneath the earth.
5|
6|For months, hunters and woodsmen have whispered about a stone doorway that appeared at the foot of a grassy hill beyond the forest. No storm uncovered it. No landslide exposed it. One morning, it simply existed. The doorway lies on an old service road once used to move ore toward [[Blacklung Quarry]].
7|
8|A dozen adventurers have entered since.
9|
10|Only one returned.
11|
12|Half-starved and barely coherent, the survivor spoke of stone guardians, corpses crawling from their tombs, and terrible glass vessels filled with swirling darkness.
13|
14|But one detail disturbed the people of [[Doobius House]] more than any other.
15|
16|He swore that after his companions died, **he could still hear them screaming from inside the tomb.**
17|
18|The tomb is the hidden laboratory of **[[Dopendis Gravebreath]]**, a necromancer and arcanist of [[Orcus]] who discovered a means of capturing mortal souls and storing them within enchanted vessels. Dopendis Gravebreath was supplied by a hidden Orcus cult operating among Stickyickistan’s mining interests; the cult sought to turn the island’s abundant [[Arcanite]] into a power source for a mass raise dead ritual.
19|
20|Dopendis Gravebreath has disappeared.
21|
22|His experiments have not.
23|
24|---
25|
26|# Adventure Hook
27|
28|The characters hear about the tomb while staying in [[Doobius House]].
29|
30|Several families are desperate to learn what happened to the missing explorers. A local scholar from the [[Seekers of the Vein]] is equally interested in the strange structure: the old service road once connected to [[Blacklung Quarry]], and the tomb’s stonework contains traces of refined [[Arcanite]]. The scholar offers the characters **100 gp** if they can determine the structure’s purpose and return with evidence.
31|
32|The sole survivor, **Bongston Vale**, can also be questioned.
33|
34|Bongston remembers little clearly, but repeatedly warns:
35|
36|> "Don't touch the jars. Gods above, don't touch the jars."
37|
38|He remembers seeing his companions die—and then hearing their voices begging him for help from somewhere deeper inside the tomb.
39|

      "content": "440|Birds return.
441|
442|Wind moves through the trees.
443|
444|Back in [[Doobius House]], the families of the missing adventurers finally learn what happened to their loved ones.
445|
446|If the characters released their souls, the community considers them heroes.
447|
448|But the discoveries within the tomb raise a much larger question. The Orcus cult did not build this laboratory for Opendis alone. They were using it as a collection site, then funneling the harvested souls and Arcanite toward the ritual beneath [[Blacklung Quarry]].
449|
450|Dopendis Gravebreath spent decades gathering souls.
451|
452|He constructed an entire laboratory.
453|
454|He created magical vessels capable of stealing the dead from the afterlife.
455|
456|And yet...
457|
458|**Dopendis Gravebreath isn't here.**
459|
460|His ritual was never completed.
461|
462|His most important research is missing.
463|
464|And one of his soul-storage crystals has already been emptied.
465|
466|Somewhere in the world, Dopendis Gravebreath may still be alive.
467|
468|And eventually, he will discover that someone has broken into his tomb.
469|
470|---
471|
472|# Scaling the Adventure
473|
474|### 3 Characters
475|
476|Remove one Animated Armor from one of the Area 3 encounters.
477|
478|The Ritual Chamber contains **2 Specters only**.
479|
480|### 4 Characters
481|
482|Run the adventure as written.
483|
484|### 5 Characters
485|
486|Run the adventure as written, but give the Ritual Chamber skeleton **2 additional Skeleton allies**.
487|
488|---
489|
490|# Adventure Rewards
491|
492|If the characters explore most of the dungeon, defeat the guardians, discover Opendis's research, and resolve the fate of the trapped souls, they have accomplished a significant adventure appropriate for 3rd level.
493|
494|Recommended rewards:
495|
496|**100 gp** from the [[Seekers of the Vein]] scholar.
497|
498|Approximately **450–700 gp worth of treasure** throughout the dungeon.
499|
500|**2 Potions of Healing.**
501|
502|**3 low-level spell scrolls.**
503|
504|Most importantly, they discover **Dopendis Gravebreath, the Orcus cult, and the Great Working**, providing a ready-made villain and plot thread for later adventures. The evidence points toward the events of [[The Tenebrous Stone-r]]: whatever the cult began beneath [[Blacklung Quarry]], the characters have only interrupted its supply line.
505|
506|## Future Hook: Dopendis Gravebreath Returns
507|
508|Don't have Opendis attack immediately.
509|
510|Weeks or even months later, the characters discover the symbol of the **hand holding the screaming skull** somewhere else.
511|
512|Perhaps on a corpse.
513|
514|Perhaps in another abandoned laboratory.
515|
516|Perhaps carried by someone asking questions about the adventurers who entered the tomb near [[Doobius House]].
517|
518|Eventually they learn the truth:
519|
520|**Dopendis Gravebreath knows their names—and the cult beneath [[Blacklung Quarry]] knows they have found the jars.**",

# Blacklung Quarry

**Blacklung Quarry** is one of [[Stickyickistan]]’s oldest and most productive sources of [[Arcanite]]. The quarry is a sprawling network of open cuts, abandoned shafts, and natural caverns on the frontier of [[The Outback]]. Its name comes from the black volcanic dust that coats the lungs of careless miners—and from the dark stone surrounding its deepest Arcanite veins.

The quarry is owned by the dwarf [[Roggan Stonebrah]], who has operated it for years with a reputation for fair wages, practical safety rules, and stubborn refusal to abandon his workers. Most of the quarry’s ore is sold through [[The Seekers of the Vein]] and eventually finds its way into Stickyickistan’s [[Magitech]] industry.

## Current Situation

The quarry ceased operations after repeated supernatural incidents. The miners first reported hearing pickaxes striking stone in shafts that had been sealed for decades. Then workers began disappearing in small groups. Every rescue party vanished as well, though the sound of mining continued each night from somewhere below.

Roggan hired **Brother Highwind** of the [[Order of the Emerald Breath]] to investigate. Brother Highwind never returned. Since his disappearance, foul-smelling [[Arcannabis]] smoke has drifted up the elevator shaft. Those who breathe it experience waking nightmares, visions of dead companions, and the sensation that something is whispering from inside their own skulls.

The disturbances are connected to the Orcus cult that once supplied [[Dopendis Gravebreath]] with Arcanite and stolen souls. After the tomb near [[Doobius House]] was abandoned, the cult moved its unfinished necromantic working beneath Blacklung Quarry. The mine’s Arcanite veins amplify the ritual, while the smoke carries psychic residue from the souls consumed below.

## Locations

### The Quarry Face

The abandoned surface works are scattered with rusting mining equipment, collapsed lifts, and piles of black stone. The air tastes metallic, and thin curls of smoke rise from cracks in the ground even when no fire burns below.

A character proficient in Nature, Investigation, or Survival can determine that some of the recent tracks belong to miners, while others are too long-strided and deep to have been made by humanoids.

### The Elevator Shaft

The main lift descends into the oldest section of the quarry. Its cables have been cut, but the platform sometimes rises by itself during the night. The shaft walls glitter with raw Arcanite and are covered in fresh pick marks that form no recognizable mining pattern.

Anyone who looks down the shaft for more than a few seconds hears a familiar voice calling their name from the darkness.

### The Sealed Workings

The deepest tunnels were closed after a cave-in generations ago. The cult reopened them from below and marked the passage with a symbol resembling **an open hand holding a screaming skull**—Dopendis Gravebreath’s seal and a blasphemous variation of the symbol of [[Orcus]].

The walls here contain fragments of glass, black wax, and silver wire. These materials match the soul-storage experiments found in Dopendis Gravebreath’s hidden laboratory.

### The Ritual Chamber

Below the sealed workings lies a natural cavern transformed into a necromantic engine. Arcanite crystals jut from the walls like black teeth, channeling energy toward a stone platform at the center. The cult has installed empty soul-storage crystals around the platform, waiting to be filled.

A thick cloud of Arcannabis smoke hangs over the chamber. It is not ordinary smoke: it contains psychic impressions from the souls used in the ritual. Creatures exposed to it may see the missing miners, hear Brother Highwind’s prayers, or mistake an ally for a corpse.

The chamber is the likely destination of the empty black crystal recovered from Dopendis Gravebreath’s laboratory. The cult’s work here is incomplete, but the quarry is already functioning as a conduit for necrotic and Arcanite energy.

## Rumors and Clues

- The miners did not all die in the tunnels. Some were taken alive for the cult’s experiments.
- The nightly pickaxe sounds are produced by undead laborers enlarging the ritual chamber.
- Brother Highwind discovered that the corruption is being fed by stolen souls, but he was captured before he could destroy the Arcanite conduit.
- Dopendis Gravebreath may have visited the quarry personally, but no one knows whether he is still beneath it.
- Destroying the central Arcanite conduit will disrupt the ritual, but may also cause the oldest tunnels to collapse.

## Adventure Connection

Blacklung Quarry is the next stage of the Orcus cult’s plan after the events of [[Jars of Souls]]. The characters may arrive here because they followed the evidence from Dopendis Gravebreath’s empty crystal, accepted Roggan Stonebrah’s bounty through [[The Rolling Papers]], or were asked by the [[Order of the Emerald Breath]] to find Brother Highwind.

The quarry can serve as the primary location for [[The Tenebrous Stone-r]]. If the characters have already explored the tomb, they recognize the cult’s seal, silver-wire circles, and soul-storage technology. If they have not, the quarry provides the first evidence that the supernatural disturbances are part of a larger Orcus conspiracy.

## Aftermath

If the characters disrupt the ritual, the smoke clears from the elevator shaft and the pickaxe sounds finally stop. The quarry remains dangerous, however: unstable tunnels, contaminated Arcanite, and surviving cult agents make reopening the mine impossible without a thorough cleansing.

Roggan Stonebrah is grateful if the miners are rescued, but he cannot afford to pay the full bounty unless the characters also secure the main workings. The Seekers of the Vein want the Arcanite recovered. The Order of the Emerald Breath wants the corrupted crystals destroyed. These demands put the characters between Stickyickistan’s hunger for magical resources and its need to prevent the cult from using them again.

### The Sealed Workings

The deepest tunnels were closed after a cave-in generations ago. The cult reopened them from below and marked the passage with a symbol resembling **an open hand holding a screaming skull**—Dopendis Gravebreath’s seal and a blasphemous variation of the symbol of [[Orcus]].

The walls here contain fragments of glass, black wax, and silver wire. These materials match the soul-storage experiments found in Dopendis Gravebreath’s hidden laboratory.

### The Ritual Chamber

Below the sealed workings lies a natural cavern transformed into a necromantic engine. Arcanite crystals jut from the walls like black teeth, channeling energy toward a stone platform at the center. The cult has installed empty soul-storage crystals around the platform, waiting to be filled.

A thick cloud of Arcannabis smoke hangs over the chamber. It is not ordinary smoke: it contains psychic impressions from the souls used in the ritual. Creatures exposed to it may see the missing miners, hear Brother Highwind’s prayers, or mistake an ally for a corpse.

The chamber is the likely destination of the empty black crystal recovered from Dopendis Gravebreath’s laboratory. The cult’s work here is incomplete, but the quarry is already functioning as a conduit for necrotic and Arcanite energy.

## Rumors and Clues

- The miners did not all die in the tunnels. Some were taken alive for the cult’s experiments.
- The nightly pickaxe sounds are produced by undead laborers enlarging the ritual chamber.
- Brother Highwind discovered that the corruption is being fed by stolen souls, but he was captured before he could destroy the Arcanite conduit.
- Dopendis Gravebreath may have visited the quarry personally, but no one knows whether he is still beneath it.
- Destroying the central Arcanite conduit will disrupt the ritual, but may also cause the oldest tunnels to collapse.

## Adventure Connection

Blacklung Quarry is the next stage of the Orcus cult’s plan after the events of [[Jars of Souls]]. The characters may arrive here because they followed the evidence from Dopendis Gravebreath’s empty crystal, accepted Roggan Stonebrah’s bounty through [[The Rolling Papers]], or were asked by the [[Order of the Emerald Breath]] to find Brother Highwind.

The quarry can serve as the primary location for [[The Tenebrous Stone-r]]. If the characters have already explored the tomb, they recognize the cult’s seal, silver-wire circles, and soul-storage technology. If they have not, the quarry provides the first evidence that the supernatural disturbances are part of a larger Orcus conspiracy.

## Aftermath

If the characters disrupt the ritual, the smoke clears from the elevator shaft and the pickaxe sounds finally stop. The quarry remains dangerous, however: unstable tunnels, contaminated Arcanite, and surviving cult agents make reopening the mine impossible without a thorough cleansing.

Roggan Stonebrah is grateful if the miners are rescued, but he cannot afford to pay the full bounty unless the characters also secure the main workings. The Seekers of the Vein want the Arcanite recovered. The Order of the Emerald Breath wants the corrupted crystals destroyed. These demands put the characters between Stickyickistan’s hunger for magical resources and its need to prevent the cult from using them again.

Mount Zooka's indigenous name is - Wachii Zookaamihk - which roughly translates to - Mountain Place of Sacred Stones.

## Blacklung Quarry

The [[Blacklung Quarry]] is one of the mountain’s oldest Arcanite-mining operations. Built into the lower slopes below the Bongstad forges, it consists of open cuts, abandoned shafts, and natural caverns following a particularly rich vein of Arcanite. Black volcanic dust gives the quarry its name, coating the lungs of careless miners and turning the surrounding stone nearly black.

The quarry was abandoned after miners began disappearing and the sound of pickaxes continued from sealed shafts. Since Brother Highwind of the [[Order of the Emerald Breath]] vanished while investigating, foul-smelling [[Arcannabis]] smoke has drifted from the elevator shaft. The quarry’s supernatural disturbances are tied to an Orcus cult using Mount Zooka’s Arcanite veins to power a necromantic ritual.

The quarry is owned by [[Roggan Stonebrah]]. Most of its ore was sold through [[The Seekers of the Vein]] and used to fuel Stickyickistan’s [[Magitech]] industry. Recovering the mine’s Arcanite now conflicts with the Order’s demand that the corrupted crystals be destroyed.

# Blacklung Quarry

**Blacklung Quarry** is one of [[Stickyickistan]]’s oldest and most productive sources of [[Arcanite]]. Located on the lower slopes of [[Mount Zooka]], the quarry consists of open cuts, abandoned shafts, and natural caverns following rich veins of ore. Black volcanic dust hangs in the air and coats the surrounding stone, giving the mine its name.

The quarry is owned by the dwarf [[Roggan Stonebrah]]. Its workers extract raw Arcanite for [[The Seekers of the Vein]], which distributes the material to Stickyickistan’s [[Magitech]] industry and forges, especially those in nearby [[Bongstad]].

The surface works are crowded with weathered mining equipment, ore carts, collapsed lifts, and black-stained stone. A deep elevator shaft descends into the oldest workings, where the walls glitter with Arcanite and the air grows hot, dusty, and difficult to breathe. The lower tunnels are unstable and have been closed several times throughout the quarry’s history.

mentionables.content:
# Adventure Hook

The characters hear about the tomb while staying in [[Doobius House]].

Several families are desperate to learn what happened to the missing explorers. A local scholar from the [[Seekers of the Vein]] is equally interested in the strange structure: the tomb’s stonework contains traces of refined [[Arcanite]], suggesting that someone transported valuable material deep into the forest. The scholar offers the characters **100 gp** if they can determine the structure’s purpose and return with evidence.

The sole survivor, **Bongston Vale**, can also be questioned.

Bongston remembers little clearly, but repeatedly warns:

> "Don't touch the jars. Gods above, don't touch the jars."

He remembers seeing his companions die—and then hearing their voices begging him for help from somewhere deeper inside the tomb.

      "content": "1|
2|> *“No permanent party, no permanent problem.”*
3|
4|[![TC_The Adventurers Guildhall Night Characters_Interior Scene.jpg](https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/v1/62750da488ff573e9bdc63c4/097ccf1b-7b44-4efd-8718-28b4da94edae/TC_The+Adventurers+Guildhall+Night+Characters_Interior+Scene.jpg)](https://www.tomcartos.com/adventurers-guildhall?itemId=tngvf4gvej5buyqrb5arpgscoykqsx)
5|
6|The **FLS Guildhall** is the informal headquarters of the [[Free League of Stickyickistan]], a loud, practical, semi-organized adventuring hub where rotating crews gather between jobs. It is less a noble institution and more a shared clubhouse, contract office, message board, tavern backroom, records archive, and monster-hunter break room all crammed under one roof.
7|
8|The guildhall serves the open-table nature of the Free League: adventurers come and go, parties form around posted jobs, DMs introduce new threats, and the setting grows through whatever survives contact with the players.
9|
10|## Overview
11|
12|**Type:** Adventurers’ guildhall / contract office / public tavern-adjacent headquarters  
13|**Location:** A grey brick road near the merchant docks on the east side of [[Nevercough Island]], [[Stickyickistan]]  
14|**Nearby:** [[Greywake Docks]]  
15|**Affiliation:** [[Free League of Stickyickistan]]  
16|**Known For:** Rotating parties, public contracts, monster hunts, shared rumors, and questionable paperwork  
17|**Primary Notice Boards:** [[The Rolling Papers]] and [[The Roach Clip]]  
18|
19|---
20|
21|## Description
22|
23|The FLS Guildhall is always busy, but rarely organized. The front room smells like rain-soaked cloaks, old paper, smoke, cheap coffee, spilled malt, floor wax, and whatever monster part someone swore was “fully preserved.” Adventurers crowd the tables between jobs, comparing scars, arguing over maps, sharpening blades, filling out forms badly, and pretending not to listen when someone else mentions a better-paying contract.
24|
25|Maps of [[Mythmos]], [[Stickyickistan]], and distant trouble spots cover the walls, many of them pinned with colored string, bounty slips, wax seals, and handwritten corrections from adventurers who survived the trip. Public contracts, civic emergencies, missing-person notices, and monster attacks circulate openly through weekly copies of [[The Rolling Papers]]. Less official opportunities drift through the room in copies of [[The Roach Clip]], whispered referrals, folded notes, and conversations that become quieter when clerks walk past.
26|
27|The guildhall does not make the Free League tidy. It makes the chaos legible. The hall exists so dangerous people can find dangerous work in a place with witnesses, paperwork, rumors, and at least a thin chance of accountability before the next disaster gets worse.
28|
29|---
30|
31|## What Adventurers Can Do Here
32|
33|- Find public adventure postings from [[The Rolling Papers]]
34|- Hear about discreet or illegal jobs from [[The Roach Clip]]
35|- Form a party for a one-shot or short arc
36|- Meet DMs, patrons, handlers, and faction contacts
37|- Research monsters, regions, and old adventure reports
38|- Buy basic adventuring supplies
39|- Arrange downtime, spellcasting services, or recovery help
40|- Report completed contracts and collect payment
41|- Display trophies, maps, warnings, and “do not touch this” items
42|
43|---
44|
45|## Important Areas
46|
47|### The Main Board
48|
49|The most visible board in the guildhall, covered in public contracts, monster warnings, missing-person notices, festival security jobs, and civic emergencies. Most jobs here are legal, public, and appropriate for adventurers who want to be paid without explaining themselves to a magistrate.
50|
51|### Weekly Papers
52|
53|Every week, fresh copies of [[The Rolling Papers]] and [[The Roach Clip]] make their way through the guildhall. The Rolling Papers are stacked openly near the Main Board, passed around over breakfast, and clipped to public contract files. The Roach Clip is less official, but just as common: folded into coat pockets, tucked between map pages, or quietly handed from one adventurer to another.
54|
55|No one needs a special shady corner to find work. Public jobs come through headlines, notices, and proper paperwork. Questionable jobs circulate through coded classifieds, rumors, dead-drop instructions, and people who know how to read between the lines.
56|
57|The guildhall does not endorse illegal work, anonymous bounties, or anything that says “do not involve the authorities,” but it also does not inspect every paper an adventurer brings inside. As long as no one causes trouble in the hall itself, the clerks let the weekly editions float around and let adventurers make their own bad decisions.
58|
59|### The Trophy Wall
60|
61|A chaotic display of monster parts, broken weapons, signed sketches, fake plaques, and real warnings. Any trophy mounted here is assumed to have a story, a smell, or a curse attached.
62|
63|### The Records Nook
64|
65|A cramped archive of past adventure reports, character records, faction notes, monster sightings, and DM scribbles. The filing system is technically alphabetical if you ask the one person who understands it.
66|
67|---
68|
69|## Services
70|
71|Guildhall services improve with a character’s Free League tier. Higher-tier adventurers have better reputations, better paperwork, and access to clerks, handlers, suppliers, and specialists who do not waste time on unproven rookies.
72|
73|### Standard Services
74|
75|| Service | Cost | Available To | Notes |
76||---|---:|---|---|
77|| Basic job registration | Free | All tiers | Lets a party claim a public contract |
78|| Contract filing | Free / small fee | All tiers | Records who accepted what and who survived |
79|| Basic supplies | At cost | All tiers | Rope, rations, torches, chalk, oil, common gear |
80|| Weekly papers | Free | All tiers | Access to circulating copies of [[The Rolling Papers]] and [[The Roach Clip]] |
81|| Rumor gathering | Drinks, tips, or favors | All tiers | Better rumors cost more than coin |
82|| [[Port Ale]] | 5 gp | All tiers | The unofficial drink of bad plans and worse sea voyages |
83|
84|### Tiered Services
85|
86|| Service | Tier 1 | Tier 2 | Tier 3 | Tier 4 |
87||---|---|---|---|---|
88|| Monster-part storage | Basic jars, cold boxes, and “please do not leak” crates | Secured cold storage and minor curse precautions | Reinforced vault space for volatile, cursed, or planar remains | Custom containment for legendary, extraplanar, or politically dangerous trophies |
89|| Spellcasting referrals | Identify, cure wounds, basic healing contacts | Lesser restoration, remove curse, dispel magic contacts | Greater restoration, divination, specialist cursebreakers | Resurrection contacts, planar experts, discreet miracle-workers |
90|| Research help | Public records and old adventure reports | Monster files, regional maps, and faction notes | Restricted archives and expert consultations | Sealed records, private briefings, and dangerous lore |
91|| Supplier access | Common adventuring gear | Uncommon consumables, silvered gear, preservation kits | Rare reagents, advanced monster-hunting gear, specialist tools | Bespoke gear, elite suppliers, and emergency procurement |
92|| Contract support | Public postings and simple paperwork | Patron verification and hazard notes | Negotiated terms, liability clauses, and faction introductions | Private commissions, diplomatic cover, and high-risk contract mediation |
93|| Recovery support | Bed, bandages, cheap food, and directions to a healer | Trusted healers and curse-removal referrals | Priority care and specialist recovery contacts | Discreet resurrection, restoration, and reputation management |
94|
95|### Notes
96|
97|- The guildhall does not provide every service directly. Many services are referrals, introductions, or access to trusted specialists.
98|- Costs are usually paid by the character unless a contract or patron covers them.
99|- [[The Roach Clip]] work does not receive official guildhall protection, even for high-tier adventurers.
100|- A character’s reputation may unlock better service, while reckless behavior may limit access regardless of tier.
101|
102|---
103|
104|## Faction Presence
105|
106|The guildhall is neutral ground in theory and a negotiation pit in practice. Representatives, recruiters, and spies from many groups pass through looking for talent.
107|
108|Possible visitors include:
109|
110|- [[Ashen Shadow Society]] bounty handlers looking for discreet monster work
111|- [[Tribunal Highblade Coalition]] officers seeking lawful mercenaries
112|- [[The Loot Tavern]] contacts interested in monster components and field reports
113|- Local nobles posting public contracts through [[The Rolling Papers]]
114|- Underworld fixers passing jobs through [[The Roach Clip]]
115|- Scholars from [[N.E.R.D]] seeking field researchers and magical samples
116|- Growers, alchemists, and merchants interested in [[Arcannabis]]-related problems
117|
118|---
119|
120|## Legal Status
121|
122|The [[Free League of Stickyickistan]] operates as a licensed adventuring exchange, not a standing army, mercenary company, or government agency. The guildhall does not command adventurers directly. Instead, it records contracts, verifies patrons when possible, tracks who accepted which job, and provides a public place where dangerous work can be offered to people reckless enough to take it.
123|
124|This arrangement exists because adventurers are already a reality in [[Stickyickistan]]. Without the guildhall, monster hunters, sell-swords, investigators, and treasure-seekers would still take jobs through taverns, alleys, noble agents, and dead drops. The Free League makes that chaos visible enough to manage. It gives authorities, patrons, and communities a place to post problems, identify who took responsibility, and hold someone accountable when things go wrong.
125|
126|The guildhall’s protection is limited. Adventurers are independent contractors. If they break the law, violate a contract, steal from clients, endanger civilians, or cause unnecessary destruction, the Free League may refuse future work, report them to the relevant authorities, or let injured parties pursue legal claims. The League can vouch that a party accepted a job; it does not automatically excuse what they do while completing it.
127|
128|Jobs from [[The Rolling Papers]] are usually public, legal, and tied to named patrons. Jobs circulating through [[The Roach Clip]] are not guildhall-endorsed, even if adventurers discuss them inside the building. The clerks do not inspect every paper, rumor, or private conversation, but any party that takes illegal work does so without the League’s protection.
129|
130|## Rules of the Hall
131|
132|1. No fighting inside the guildhall.
133|2. No stealing contracts, payments, gear, trophies, or monster parts.
134|3. No live monsters inside the hall without permission and restraints.
135|4. No cursed, diseased, explosive, or whispering items left unattended.
136|5. Public contracts require names, witnesses, and a clerk’s mark.
137|6. Roach Clip work is not protected by guildhall paperwork.
138|7. If you damage the hall, frighten the clerk, or start a faction incident, you pay for it.
139|8. Parties are temporary. Reputations are not.
140|",

# Adventure Hook

The characters hear about the tomb while staying in [[Doobius House]].

Several families are desperate to learn what happened to the missing explorers. A local scholar from the [[Seekers of the Vein]] is equally interested in the strange structure: the tomb’s stonework contains traces of refined [[Arcanite]], suggesting that someone transported valuable material deep into the forest. The scholar offers the characters **100 gp** if they can determine the structure’s purpose and return with evidence.

The sole survivor, **Bongston Vale**, can also be questioned.

Bongston remembers little clearly, but repeatedly warns:

> "Don't touch the jars. Gods above, don't touch the jars."

He remembers seeing his companions die—and then hearing their voices begging him for help from somewhere deeper inside the tomb.
value.newText:
# Adventure Hook

The characters begin at the [[FLS Guildhall]] on [[Nevercough Island]], looking for work through the [[Free League of Stickyickistan]]. A public notice on [[The Rolling Papers]] offers **100 gp** to investigate a newly revealed tomb in the wooded interior of [[The Outback]] and return with evidence of its purpose.

The notice was posted by a scholar working with [[The Seekers of the Vein]]. The scholar believes the tomb’s stonework contains traces of refined [[Arcanite]], suggesting that someone transported valuable material deep into the forest. Several families from [[Doobius House]] have also contacted the Guildhall, desperate to learn what happened to the missing explorers.

The sole survivor, **Bongston Vale**, is being cared for at the Guildhall’s recovery rooms and can be questioned before the party leaves. Bongston remembers little clearly, but repeatedly warns:

> "Don't touch the jars. Gods above, don't touch the jars."

He remembers seeing his companions die—and then hearing their voices begging him for help from somewhere deeper inside the tomb.

## The Roach Clip Hook: Unfinished Business

Characters who took part in [[The Tenebrous Stone-r]] may find a second notice in [[The Roach Clip]], tucked behind the public posting or passed to them by a quiet Guildhall contact. The coded notice reads:

> **The mountain’s dead are still being moved. Find the missing shipment before it reaches the forest. Ask about the jars. Tell no one in a uniform.**

The Roach Clip contact believes the tomb is connected to the same Orcus cult and soul-powered experiments encountered beneath [[Blacklung Quarry]]. The party is not being asked to investigate openly; they are being asked to determine whether the cult is still operating, recover any evidence, and prevent the shipment from reaching another site.

This hook is ideal for returning characters from [[The Tenebrous Stone-r]]. They recognize the cult’s methods, the smell of corrupted [[Arcannabis]], or the traces of Arcanite used in the tomb’s construction. The public 100 gp reward remains available, but the Roach Clip contact may offer an additional **100 gp** for keeping the connection to [[Blacklung Quarry]] quiet—or for recovering a usable cult insignia, soul-storage component, or other evidence.

# Adventure Hook

The characters begin at the [[FLS Guildhall]] on [[Nevercough Island]], looking for work through the [[Free League of Stickyickistan]]. A public notice on [[The Rolling Papers]] offers **100 gp** to investigate a newly revealed tomb in the wooded interior of [[The Outback]] and return with evidence of its purpose.

The notice was posted by a scholar working with [[The Seekers of the Vein]]. The scholar believes the tomb’s stonework contains traces of refined [[Arcanite]], suggesting that someone transported valuable material deep into the forest. Several families from [[Doobius House]] have also contacted the Guildhall, desperate to learn what happened to the missing explorers.

The sole survivor, **Bongston Vale**, is being cared for at the Guildhall’s recovery rooms and can be questioned before the party leaves. Bongston remembers little clearly, but repeatedly warns:

> "Don't touch the jars. Gods above, don't touch the jars."

He remembers seeing his companions die—and then hearing their voices begging him for help from somewhere deeper inside the tomb.

## The Roach Clip Hook: Unfinished Business

Characters who took part in [[The Tenebrous Stone-r]] may find a second notice in [[The Roach Clip]], tucked behind the public posting or passed to them by a quiet Guildhall contact. The coded notice reads:

> **The mountain’s dead are still being moved. Find the missing shipment before it reaches the forest. Ask about the jars. Tell no one in a uniform.**

The Roach Clip contact believes the tomb is connected to the same Orcus cult and soul-powered experiments encountered beneath [[Blacklung Quarry]]. The party is not being asked to investigate openly; they are being asked to determine whether the cult is still operating, recover any evidence, and prevent the shipment from reaching another site.

This hook is ideal for returning characters from [[The Tenebrous Stone-r]]. They recognize the cult’s methods, the smell of corrupted [[Arcannabis]], or the traces of Arcanite used in the tomb’s construction. The public 100 gp reward remains available, but the Roach Clip contact may offer an additional **100 gp** for keeping the connection to [[Blacklung Quarry]] quiet—or for recovering a usable cult insignia, soul-storage component, or other evidence.

value.newText:
## The Roach Clip Hook: Unfinished Business

Characters who took part in [[The Tenebrous Stone-r]] may find a second notice in [[The Roach Clip]], tucked behind the public posting or passed to them by a quiet Guildhall contact. The coded notice reads:

> **The mountain’s dead are still being moved. Find the missing shipment before it reaches the forest. Ask about the jars. Tell no one in a uniform.**

The Roach Clip contact believes the tomb is connected to the same Orcus cult and soul-powered experiments encountered beneath [[Blacklung Quarry]]. The party is asked to recover the intact Jars of Souls and deliver them to a discreet buyer before the cult can reclaim them. The buyer wants the jars **untouched**—do not break them, release the spirits, or damage the vessels.

Bongston Vale’s warning is therefore exactly what the buyer wants the characters to ignore:

> **“Touch the jars. Bring me every one you can carry.”**

The buyer offers **500 gp for each intact Jar of Souls recovered**, up to **2,000 gp** for the four active jars in the ritual chamber. They also pay a **500 gp bonus** if the characters return with an additional intact jar from the earlier chambers, making this a far more lucrative proposition than simply destroying the vessels. The public 100 gp reward remains available, but accepting the Roach Clip contract means the characters are expected to collect the jars rather than smash them.

This hook is ideal for returning characters from [[The Tenebrous Stone-r]]. They may recognize the cult’s methods, the smell of corrupted [[Arcannabis]], or the traces of Arcanite used in the tomb’s construction. The buyer’s identity is deliberately concealed; they may be a rival cultist, a forbidden-magic collector, or someone who wants the souls for purposes even worse than the Orcus ritual.

## The Roach Clip Hook: Unfinished Business

Characters who took part in [[The Tenebrous Stone-r]] may find a second notice in [[The Roach Clip]], tucked behind the public posting or passed to them by a quiet Guildhall contact. The coded notice reads:

> **The mountain’s dead are still being moved. Find the missing shipment before it reaches the forest. Ask about the jars. Tell no one in a uniform.**

The Roach Clip contact believes the tomb is connected to the same Orcus cult and soul-powered experiments encountered beneath [[Blacklung Quarry]]. The party is asked to recover the intact Jars of Souls and deliver them to a discreet buyer before the cult can reclaim them. The buyer wants the jars **untouched**—do not break them, release the spirits, or damage the vessels.

Bongston Vale’s warning is therefore exactly what the buyer wants the characters to ignore:

> **“Touch the jars. Bring me every one you can carry.”**

The buyer offers **500 gp for each intact Jar of Souls recovered**, up to **2,000 gp** for the four active jars in the ritual chamber. They also pay a **500 gp bonus** if the characters return with an additional intact jar from the earlier chambers, making this a far more lucrative proposition than simply destroying the vessels. The public 100 gp reward remains available, but accepting the Roach Clip contract means the characters are expected to collect the jars rather than smash them.

This hook is ideal for returning characters from [[The Tenebrous Stone-r]]. They may recognize the cult’s methods, the smell of corrupted [[Arcannabis]], or the traces of Arcanite used in the tomb’s construction. The buyer’s identity is deliberately concealed; they may be a rival cultist, a forbidden-magic collector, or someone who wants the souls for purposes even worse than the Orcus ritual.

value.newText:
[[Skarguther Dungleboof]], the CFO of the Stickyickistanian [[Dungsweepers]], a member of the [[Heralds of Dust]], and a collector of cursed and unholy relics, is the Roach Clip contact and buyer. He is a powerful and well-connected Duster with a particular interest in the undead and the treatment of trapped souls. Skarguther heard about the Orcus cult and soul-powered experiments beneath [[Blacklung Quarry]], and believes the mysterious tomb of "jars" is connected to them. He wants the party to recover the intact Jars of Souls and deliver them to him before the cult can reclaim them—not to use the souls as fuel, but to remove them from the cult’s reach and study how they might be guided toward [[Heralds of Dust|True Death]].

Skarguther is not necessarily a bad man. The Dusters believe death is a passage toward True Death, and he considers leaving tortured souls sealed inside necromantic vessels an ongoing atrocity. However, his methods are often outside the law: he acquires cursed relics through the black market, conceals dangerous evidence from authorities, and keeps undead or spiritually contaminated objects in unofficial collections. He wants the jars **fully intact** because smashing them may release the souls violently or destroy the evidence needed to understand their condition.

messages.content:
Updated the [[The Roach Clip]] hook to clarify Skarguther’s motives:

- He wants the jars because they contain **tortured souls**, not simply because they are valuable relics.
- As a member of the [[Heralds of Dust]], he wants to remove the souls from the Orcus cult’s reach and study how they might be guided toward [[Heralds of Dust|True Death]].
- He is **not necessarily evil** and considers the jars an ongoing atrocity.
- His methods remain illegal or ethically questionable because he deals in black-market relics, conceals evidence, and maintains unofficial collections of undead and spiritually contaminated objects.
- He wants the jars intact because smashing them could release the souls violently or destroy evidence needed to understand their condition.
